To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the computerized analysis and interpretation of transverse pore gradients is a powerful tool for the detection of DNA anomalies.

(i) computerized analysis of Ferguson curves provides precise and rapid determination of KR and YO values; and (ii) the KR and YO parameters are highly informative for the analysis of DNA restriction fragments in transverse pore gradient poly-acrylamide gels.

1) the computerized analysis is a rapid and precise method for the determination of KR and YO values from Ferguson curves; 2) these parameters are highly correlated with the electrophoretic mobility of the DNA fragments; 3) the KR value is a sensitive and quantitative parameter that can detect anomalously migrating DNA fragments; and 4) the computerized method is limited to intra-experiment comparisons of Ferguson curves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative, rapid and sensitive method for the detection of anomalously migrated DNA species.
the application of transverse pore gradients to the separation and detection of DNA restriction fragments.
a method for computer-aided analysis for the rapid quantitative interpretation and detection of anomalous migration in DNA restriction fragments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the computerized analysis provides a rapid, sensitive, precise and objective method for the quantitative detection of anomalously-migrating DNA species in transverse pore gradient poly-acrylamide gels.
the computer-aided analysis is a powerful tool for the quantitative interpretation of Ferguson curve patterns.

computerized analysis of Ferguson curves provides a more precise and accurate method of analysis of DNA restriction fragments on transverse pore gradient poly-acrylamide gels than the conventional methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
computer-aided analysis has provided a means for rapid, quantitative interpretation of Ferguson curve patterns.
transverse pore gradient gel electrophoreses of DNA restriction fragments provides a sensitive and informative method to detect anomalous DNA migration.
computer-aided curve analysis is an effective method to analyze Ferguson curves and that the method can be readily implemented on a personal computer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
computerized analysis is a powerful tool for rapid quantitative interpretation of transverse pore gradients.
computerized curve analysis is a powerful tool for the quantitative interpretation of Ferguson plots.
the Ferguson curve is an excellent tool for detecting anomalous DNA migration and for characterizing DNA molecules in terms of size, charge, shape and conformation.
